title: Heterogeneity of treatment effect of transcatheter tricuspid intervention by baseline risk, using reconstructed and trial-level data from the randomised trials, timed to the next pivotal readouts

pico.population: Adults with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation randomised to transcatheter tricuspid repair or replacement versus medical therapy
pico.intervention: Tricuspid TEER or transcatheter valve replacement
pico.comparator: Medical therapy (and, indirectly, each device against the other)
pico.outcomes: Death, heart failure hospitalisation, tricuspid surgery, KCCQ, bleeding and pacemaker implantation, analysed as time-to-event components and win-ratio hierarchies

decision: Which patients with severe TR should be offered T-TEER, TTVR or continued medical therapy, and when
decision_maker: Heart teams and interventional cardiologists; guideline committees
why_now: Four randomised comparisons against medical therapy have reported (PMIDs 39471883, 39602173, 39475399, 42670975) with primary results expressed as win ratios, while component effects on death and HF hospitalisation look weaker (39471883, 36876753). Further pivotal RCTs read out from 2027 (NCT04097145).

competing.note: CLASP II TR randomised pivotal trial; would add to pooled evidence, not answer HTE alone

gap_type: underpowered trials and effect modification not testable within single trials

designs.primary: Reconstructed-IPD and trial-level meta-analysis of randomised trials with Bayesian network synthesis across T-TEER and TTVR, win-ratio and time-to-event components, and risk-stratified effect modelling; protocol on PROSPERO before the next readout with a pre-specified living update
designs.alternative: One-stage IPD meta-analysis through data-sharing agreements with the trial sponsors and steering committees

data_required: Published Kaplan-Meier curves and subgroup tables from the randomised trials; IPD if sponsors share. Pooled inputs: 572 (39471883) + 300 (39602173) + 400 (39475399) + 360 (42670975) = 1,632 participants, before resolving any overlap with 36876753 (350 randomised).
feasibility: Reconstructed-IPD NMA is within the owner's methods; true IPD requires sponsor cooperation and win-ratio hierarchies cannot be fully reconstructed from published curves.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects; shares method with the STEMI reconstructed-IPD NMA.

G1.note: Decision between intervention and medical therapy in a common, high-morbidity condition; hard components are death and HF hospitalisation.

G2.note: Component effects on death and HF hospitalisation appear weaker than composite win ratios in 36876753 and 39471883, and 40159089 reports a lower recurrent HF hospitalisation rate at 2 years, so benefit by subgroup is unresolved. Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved), so equipoise is judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No meta-analysis of these trials is in the appraised subset (subset only; not verified against the full store). NCT04097145 (n=1270, primary completion 2027-12-31) will add to the pooled evidence but cannot answer cross-trial effect modification alone; re-check before registration.

G4.note: A pre-registered synthesis with explicit risk stratification is citable by a guideline committee, and single trials cannot test effect modification across devices.

G5.note: Tests effect modification and indirect device comparison rather than repeating a pooled main effect; risk of being read as a repeat if it reports only pooled win ratios.

impact.why: Severe TR is common in older patients and the device decision is increasingly frequent.

novelty.why: Pooled main effects are likely to be published by others; the HTE and indirect comparison angle is less so.

equipoise.why: Composite benefit is shown, while component and subgroup effects are uncertain.

design.why: Reconstruction cannot recover win-ratio hierarchies, which limits credibility without IPD.

timeliness.why: Several pivotal readouts fall in 2027 to 2029 (NCT04097145, NCT06458907).

citation.why: Trial-based syntheses in target journals attract moderate citation, uncalibrated until the benchmark is complete.

feasibility.why: Aligned with the owner's reconstructed-IPD workflow.

next_actions: Search the full store for existing tricuspid meta-analyses and confirm G3
Draft and register a PROSPERO protocol with pre-specified living update
Extract published curves, subgroup tables and win-ratio components from the four RCTs and decide overlap with 36876753

title: Transcatheter versus isolated surgical intervention for severe tricuspid regurgitation: target trial emulation in national registries

pico.population: Adults with isolated severe tricuspid regurgitation judged suitable for either transcatheter or surgical intervention
pico.outcomes: All-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalisation, stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, reintervention
pico.timing: 30 days to 5 years from time zero

decision: Whether to refer an operable patient with isolated severe TR for transcatheter or surgical intervention
decision_maker: Heart teams, cardiac surgeons and interventional cardiologists
why_now: Surgical series report no survival benefit over medical therapy overall (31071413, HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.78 to 2.30; 39212387, HR .97, 95% CI .88-1.08), yet randomised transcatheter trials compare only against medical therapy (39471883, 39475399), leaving no comparative evidence between the two routes in the appraised subset.

competing.note: Band versus ring, surgical comparison only
Transcatheter replacement versus control; not versus surgery

designs.primary: Target trial emulation with clone-censor-weight or propensity methods in linked national hospital and procedure registries
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial of transcatheter versus surgical strategy in low-to-intermediate surgical risk patients

data_required: Linked national procedure, hospital and mortality data with echocardiographic severity and TRI-SCORE components; sufficient transcatheter volume.
feasibility: Not available to the owner today; requires a registry collaboration, and echocardiographic severity is rarely captured in administrative data.

G1.note: Common decision in a high-morbidity population, judged on mortality and HF hospitalisation.

G2.note: No comparative evidence between routes; surgery shows no clear survival gain overall (31071413, 39212387). Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved), so equipoise is judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No randomised transcatheter-versus-surgery comparison appears in the trials file.

G4.note: Confounding by indication and immortal time are severe, and unmeasured anatomy and RV function may be unrecoverable from registries; credibility depends on data not yet identified, so the gate is not met until a dataset is confirmed.

G5.note: Not a repeat synthesis and not surrogate-only.

impact.why: Smaller patient pool than the medical-therapy question.

novelty.why: No comparative evidence appears in the subset.

timeliness.why: Transcatheter use is growing, but no single trigger.

citation.why: Emulation studies in target journals are cited moderately.

next_actions: Identify registries with linked TR severity and procedure type
Specify the target trial protocol, time zero and estimand
Confirm that no comparative study exists in the full store

status_history.reason: Generated from D5 landscape synthesis; G4 not met

title: Cost-effectiveness and value of information of tricuspid TEER and transcatheter valve replacement for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation in the UK health system

pico.population: Patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation on medical therapy
pico.comparator: Medical therapy, and each device against the other
pico.outcomes: QALYs, costs, incremental net monetary benefit, expected value of perfect and partial perfect information

decision: Reimbursement and the priority for further trials, including whether a head-to-head or long-term mortality trial is justified
decision_maker: Health technology assessment bodies and funders; heart teams
why_now: Randomised trials report win-ratio composites with bleeding and pacemaker costs (39475399: severe bleeding 15.4% vs 5.3%), while component effects on mortality are uncertain, so value depends on extrapolation.

competing.note: Pivotal randomised trial that will update inputs

designs.primary: Patient-level Markov microsimulation with probabilistic sensitivity analysis and value-of-information analysis
designs.alternative: Partitioned survival model with network meta-analysis inputs

data_required: Trial outcomes and utilities, UK procedure and device costs, long-term survival of untreated TR (31071413, 39212387).
feasibility: Matches the owner's microsimulation methods; costs and utilities need collaborators.
overlap: Methodological overlap only with the Impella STEMI-CS microsimulation; no duplication.

G1.note: Informs funding of a frequent procedure with substantial costs.

G2.note: Long-term mortality effect is uncertain from the reported component results. Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved), so equipoise is judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No economic evaluation is in the appraised subset; not verified against the full store, and NCT04097145 would update inputs after 2027.

G4.note: Value-of-information outputs size a future trial, and economic analyses are cited by assessment bodies.

G5.note: Not a repeat synthesis; but risk of being judged a subspecialty or health-economics paper rather than a parent-journal one.

impact.why: Procedure growth and cost give moderate system impact.

novelty.why: Economic evaluation after RCTs is expected from others.

citation.why: Cost-effectiveness papers are less cited in parent journals.

feasibility.why: Methods already held by the owner.

next_actions: Confirm no published economic evaluation in the full store
Define model structure and extract transition inputs
Agree costing sources with a health economist collaborator

status_history.reason: Generated from D5 landscape synthesis; likely subspecialty ceiling
